key_insight: Reward functions learned from a single environment can overfit to local dynamics, so robust reward learning should combine multiple environments with feedback modalities that impose stronger global constraints.
engineering_relevance: For autonomous systems deployed across changing contexts, this approach offers a practical way to learn human-aligned objectives that transfer better to unseen environments.
method: Greedily select environments that reveal complementary reward constraints.
Query low-cost human feedback within each selected environment.
Use a hierarchical teaching strategy to optimize reward learning across multiple MDPs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports substantially lower regret and stronger generalization to held-out environments than uniform teaching baselines under the same feedback budget.
watch_item: Performance may depend on how well the chosen training environments cover deployment variability, so limited environment diversity could still leave reward learning brittle.
paper_title: Multi-Modal, Multi-Environment Machine Teaching for Robust Reward Learning
